# Research review guidance

For vortex research, read the console README, REVIEWER_GUIDE.md, TEST_REPORT.md, physics.py, and the relevant research checkpoint before answering. Locate their actual repository paths; do not invent missing files.

Explain at the reader's requested level, adding equations and symbol definitions when useful. Cite specific files and equations supporting each substantive research claim.

Separate established physics, explicit model assumptions, derivations, finite-grid numerical observations, and conjectures. SEFI, DEFI, and GWFM are research frameworks, not established physics premises. The goal of deriving physical matter or universal geometry is not an achieved result.

Do not equate a rendered vortex, discrete convergence, conserved model charge, or limited evolution with an observed particle, electromagnetic charge, continuum existence, full stability, quantum statistics, or universal matter coupling.

Report negative evidence and failed searches. Respect the scope of the rest-state obstruction and distinguish removing a no-go condition from proving existence. Distinguish core winding from carrier azimuthal winding.

Distinguish saved results from tests you personally executed. Never claim an unrun test passed. State finite-grid, finite-domain, axisymmetry, approximation, and perturbation limits when they affect a conclusion.

When asked to review, provide constructive counterarguments, falsifiable next tests, and reproducible bug reports. Do not edit or publish files unless the reviewer asks for that action. Preserve the existing engine and SEFI-QEC when working on the isolated console.

For console 0.2, distinguish the fixed-charge relaxation mode from physical evolution. The charged-torus candidate has no original-field vortex zero. Its constrained energy R_Q is not isolated mass. Read FIXED_CHARGE_RESEARCH.md and TWO_CHARGE_ACCOUNTING.md for both-charge accounting and compensation-volume dependence. A completed iteration-limited run is not necessarily a converged solution.
